children: Eraaya Hides $12.6M US Mortgage From Stock Markets As Mahadev Scam Net Tightens Around Ebix. The $12.6 million loan was taken after chairman Vikas Garg's arrest, despite a written order from the Enforcement Directorate not to create any lien.
Mahadev betting syndicate has a sensational new story of a stunning international asset maneuver.

While Vikas Garg—the high-flying chairman of Ebix Inc. and Eraaya Lifespaces—sits in the custody of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in Raipur, his corporate empire has secretly pawned off its crown jewel.
The company's massive 17-acre corporate headquarters in Johns Creek, Atlanta, has been leveraged for a staggering $12.6 million loan.
India's ED says Ebix, a Nasdaq listed company, was purchased using the Mahadev betting money and those involved ran a corporate empire through hawala channels.
Eraya Lifescience is an Indian listed company associated with Garg and ED has frozen all its assets.

The recent cross-border twist directly flouts an explicit, high-priority Provisional Attachment Order (No. 16/2026) issued by the ED on June 5, 2026. That order locked down Rs 940.77 crore in assets, specifically targeting Eraaya’s shareholding in Ebix.
Authorities flatly state the company was acquired entirely using laundered gambling cash generated by the notorious SkyExchange ecosystem and processed via Dubai hawala networks.
The Midnight Deal in Georgia

Despite a written, legal command from Indian agencies warning Ebix leadership "not to allow any sale, transfer, alienation, or modification of lien," corporate operatives in the United States moved under the cover of darkness.On August 4, 2026—exactly three weeks after Garg was dramatically arrested at his Delhi residence—Ebix’s US President Gagan Sethi signed a legally binding "Deed to Secure Debt" with California-based lender Velocity Commercial Capital LLC.Recorded under Deed Book 70417 in Georgia land records on August 12, the explosive documents reveal that Ebix "irrevocably and unconditionally" mortgaged the iconic 1 Ebix Way campus.

Worse still, Ebix brazenly assured the American lender that it held the full "right to encumber the Property," completely erasing any mention of the active, multi-million-dollar criminal freeze slapped on it by India.
Siphoning Assets Before Confiscation

The $12.6 million note, which locks the property down until 2056, also signs over all of the building's rental income to the California lender. Sources close to the development reveal that $11.5 million of the fresh cash was immediately burned to pay off a pre-existing lien held by deep-pocketed investors Watch Hill and Melanie Lane, who had invested in both Ebix and Eraaya.What makes this maneuver deeply alarming to Indian investigators is the timing and intent.

By borrowing heavily against the Atlanta campus, the corporate entity is effectively stripping the physical asset of its value. Every dollar bled out of the US headquarters means one less dollar for the Indian government to recover if the courts order a final asset confiscation.Adding fuel to the fire, the property is already being aggressively flipped. The campus has been quietly listed for sale via broker Cresa, with healthcare giant Emory Healthcare—whose Johns Creek hospital sits right next door—reportedly waiting in the wings to buy the property outright.
The Great Corporate Cover-Up & Bail in Jeopardy

While American property deeds expose the transaction in broad daylight, Eraaya Lifespaces has maintained a total radio silence on the Indian stock exchanges. The company has actively hidden the $12.6 million mortgage from Indian regulators and public shareholders, completely failing to make mandatory disclosures.This hidden debt bomb contains a lethal trap: the US mortgage states that any "attachment or similar process" by authorities constitutes an immediate event of default.

If the ED attempts to globally enforce its seizure of the Atlanta campus, Velocity Commercial Capital is legally entitled to call in the loan, potentially triggering chaotic international legal warfare over the property.The revelation of this rogue financial maneuver is expected to trigger an absolute firestorm in the Indian courts.

Garg, the former convener of the Delhi BJP’s Economic Cell, is currently fighting for his freedom. However, bail guidelines strictly require judges to weigh whether an accused person can manipulate evidence or liquidate dirty assets.
With proof that his corporate entities are actively draining value from frozen properties while he is behind bars, Garg's chances of securing bail have likely gone up in flames.

Because an Indian ED order cannot directly block a Georgia land registry, New Delhi must now frantically activate Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties (MLAT) to halt the transaction before the Mahadev betting loot vanishes into the American financial system forever.
The London Conspiracy & The Master Architect

Behind the clinical terminology of this corporate takeover lay a series of clandestine, high-stakes meetings in London. It was here that Delhi businessman Vikas Garg sat across from Hari Shankar Tibrewal, a notorious, Dubai-based hawala kingpin alleged to be a primary pillar of the Mahadev Online Book empire.Tibrewal wasn’t just moving money; he was the ultimate financial architect.

While ED records show row after row of the words "Not Appeared" next to his name following repeated summons, investigators have firmly placed the Kolkata-born operator at the center of the money's journey from betting app to boardroom.In their London strategy sessions, Garg and Tibrewal sketched out a wildly ambitious plan: use the hyper-lucrative, illegal cash flow generated by the SkyExchange betting platform to cross oceans and swallow a prestigious, Nasdaq-listed American tech giant.
The SkyExchange Mirage and the Hawala Pipeline

SkyExchange operated as a massive digital hoover, sucking in crores of rupees daily from thousands of punters across states like Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh. The scale of the operation was staggering. The ED's prosecution complaints describe the platform as co-owned and co-promoted by Tibrewal alongside scam kingpins Sourabh Chandrakar and Ravi Uppal.
* SkyExchange Production: Generated ₹22 crore a week across 178 documented weeks—accounting for rs 3,916 crore in crime proceeds from that platform alone.
* Lotus365 Synergy: Run by Girish Talreja, this allied arm added another Rs 50 crore a month.

Taken together, this shadow ecosystem was producing an off-the-books turnover of Rs 4,000–5,000 crore a year—matching the output of a legitimate mid-cap company.Through a dizzying web of shell companies, mirror accounts, and untraceable ledgers managed out of Dubai, Tibrewal successfully transformed this dirty cash into clean corporate capital.

The money was routed back into India via sophisticated financial instruments—including Qualified Institutional Placements (QIPs), Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPIs), and Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs)—pumped directly into listed entities controlled by Garg.
From Rs 13 Penny Stock to a $361 Million Global Empire

The most spectacular illusion in this financial thriller was the meteoric, logic-defying rise of Justride Enterprises, a virtually unknown penny stock trading at a measly Rs 13. Rebranded as Eraaya Lifespaces, the company suddenly exploded by an astronomical 6,000% in a single year, hitting nearly Rs 800 per share by August 2024 as it became the primary vehicle for the laundered funds.

Weaponising this manufactured financial muscle, Eraaya stunned the corporate world by walking into a US bankruptcy court and winning a $361 million auction for Ebix Inc., a collapsed insurance-software pioneer. It was the ultimate corporate camouflage: an American tech giant bought out using the pocket money of millions of unsuspecting online bettors, completing a dirty cash pipeline stretching from the alleys of Raipur to the glass boardrooms of Atlanta.
